description: Osmotic cementitious mortar suitable for contact with drinking water, for waterproofing masonry and concrete structures
whereToUse: Repairing underground masonries subject to water and moisture seepage in situations with negative pressure up to 1 atmosphere.
Waterproofing basins, reservoirs, concrete or masonry tanks and pipes containing drinking water.
Waterproofing concrete or masonry tanks containing sewage water
notFor: Do not use Planiseal 88 for solving internal condensation problems (use de-humidifying renders, improve ventilation to the area or provide adequate insulation).
Do not use on plasters, plasterboards, painted walls, plywood, chipboard, asbestos cement.
Do not use on surfaces subject to dynamic stresses
In no case should Planiseal 88 be applied to a substrate that shows signs of standing water on the surface
Even though Planiseal 88 is resistant to abrasion and wear from solids normally present in liquids flowing in hydraulic structures, it must not be exposed to traffic.

standards.value: conforms to the requirements of EN 1504-2 coating (C) according to the MC and IR principles
Planiseal 88 corresponds to the principles defined in EN 1504-9
Planiseal 88 is certified to AS/NZS 4020:2018 for use with potable water.

consumption.basis: per m2 per mm of thickness (no application method specified)
consumption.quote: approx. 1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness.

mixing: Pour 4.2 - 4.6 litres of water into a suitable container and slowly add the Planiseal 88 while blending with a mechanical mixer.
storage: Planiseal 88 may be stored for up to 12 months in its original packaging in a dry, elevated area.
notes: The sheet gives one consumption figure only (approx. 1.5 kg/m2 per mm of thickness), not split by brush, trowel or spray, and gives no total per m2; the required final thickness is 'approximately 2-3 mm' in all cases. Coats: brush 2-3 coats, spray two layers; for trowel no number of coats is stated, only that a first coat by brush is recommended. Waiting time between coats is worded two ways: body text 'generally 5-6 hours ... not to exceed 24 hours', table 'after 5 hours, and no later than 24 hours'. The mixing sentence gives 4.2 - 4.6 litres of water without saying per bag; the table row gives '21-23% (4.2 - 4.6) per 20 kg bag' without a unit on the 4.2 - 4.6. Final performance figures are stated for 22% mixing water at 2.5 mm thickness. The bond strength label is printed 'MC 0.40 - water/cement ratio' in the layout extraction and without the dash in the reading-order extraction; the label recorded follows the reading-order text. Performance-table cells are split across lines in both extractions, so the vapour permeability value is recorded only as 'SD < 1 Class I'. The limit 'it can only be used for rigid waterproofing' and the requirement to protect floors with a 4-5 cm thick cementitious screed are in the sheet but not in notFor (five-item cap). This is the Mapei Australia edition of the sheet.
